title: openai-chat-completions: parity for roles/stop/logprobs + streaming & structured output
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: bring /v1/chat.completions compatibility parity for Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR implements correct handling of message roles, stop sequences, logprobs request/response plumbing, structured output formatting, and stabilizes streaming for function/tool calling. Summary of changes: 1) request parsing now accepts role values (system/user/assistant/tool) and maps them to internal message types preserving metadata, 2) 'stop' can accept string|array and is applied both at tokenizer and streaming boundary checks, 3) logprobs support toggles token-level scoring and is propagated from the API surface to the runtime evaluator, 4) structured output and response_format handling added so that the compatibility layer can accept formatting hints and emit the same JSON/string shapes as OpenAI, 5) streaming stability fixes for function/tool calls including chunk boundary alignment, partial function call payload buffering, and backpressure-safe flushing. Includes unit + integration tests and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Implement request field mapping and validation - [x] Wire stop handling to tokenizer/streamer - [x] Propagate logprobs flag to runtime + tests - [x] Structured output serialization and example tests - [x] Streaming stability e2e for function calls - [x] Update SDK tests and examples - [x] Add release notes and Linear links. Related: Linear ENG-3245, ENG-3301. A few behavioural notes: compatibility layer will return truncated function call payloads only if the streaming connection closes early; stop sequences are applied before logprobs computation to match OpenAI ordering; role 'tool' is accepted and forwarded as-is. Breaking changes: none expected for existing Redwood API users; this only expands the compatibility layer.
